brief: Goldman's mid-day US equities color for 17 Sep 2026 describes a broad risk rally. Treasury yields and WTI fall after Saudi Arabia eases oil supply constraints (the East-West pipeline restarts and ship-to-ship transfers increase), letting SPX reclaim its 50-day average (7615) after bouncing off the 100-day average (7515) in the prior session, with VIX back to a 15 handle. MegaCap Tech (+100bps) remains the desk's high-conviction trade. TMT was the most net-bought US sector over the past month on hyperscaler longs, pushing Mag 7 net allocation to about 20% (95th percentile, three-year) from a June low of 14%. Momentum, AI semis, AI leaders and short-covering baskets all post double-digit gains, a squeezy tilt to the tape. Liquidity is thin (top-of-book down 50% versus the 5-day average) even as volume runs 31% above the 20-day average, and CTAs are modeled to sell $30bn over the next week in a flat tape. Separately, GIR reads yesterday's FOMC hike as more hawkish than its prior view: a 16-2 majority penciled in another hike this year, no dissents against the hike itself, the neutral rate dot rose to 3.25%, and Chairman Warsh repeated that the hike removed a dose of accommodation.
